newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-WARNE TIRING AT THE TOP.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WARNE TIRING AT THE TOP.

text.p: Australia's master leg-spinner Shane Warne is tiring of the rigours of test cricket and says he may retire within a few years.
The 27-year-old bowler told Melbourne's Herald-Sun newspaper he had no intention of dragging out his career until a loss of form or fitness forced him out.
"It's not injuries, it's the pressure," Warne said from Cape Town after Australia's third limited overs international against South Africa.
"There is that much pressure on and I don't know that I can stay at the mental level required to achieve the performance that I and everyone else wants for the next four or five years.
"I have never been a guy who was going to play until I was 35 or 40."

Warne has taken 240 wickets in 52 tests and is seen as a potential Australia test captain. After their 2-1 test series win against South Africa, Australia leave next month for a six-test series against England.
"This could be my last Ashes tour so I really want to make it a big one," Warne said.
"By the time the next Ashes tour comes around (in 2001) I will be 31 or 32 and there is a big chance I might be looking for other things in life."
